subject: Follow-up: connection pooling thresholds, concurrency targets, and credits
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Seth Li <seth.li@fastledger.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: connection pooling thresholds, concurrency targets, and credits

Hi Seth — great talk this morning. Thanks for walking through FastLedger's ingestion and realtime reconciliation workload. Quick recap and suggested next steps below so we can align on SLOs and a pilot capacity plan.

Call recap
- Primary workload: reconciliation pipelines that fan out to external partners and then stream results back to FastLedger’s UI.
- Target latency: P95 generation <= 300ms for short completions (~<200 tokens); P95 streaming tail within 400ms for end-to-end UI updates.
- Sustained throughput: ~200 rps; expected peak bursts up to 800 rps for 2–3 minute intervals during batch close.
- Concurrency/connection model: roughly 180 concurrent long-lived streaming connections (websocket-style), plus ~600 short-lived parallel requests for batch fanout during peaks.
- Important: connection reuse and HTTP/2 multiplexing are possible on your side; you asked about per-connection limits and burst tokens from Redwood.

What Redwood proposes (high-level)
- Default hosted plan limits: per-tenant concurrency window enforced at routing layer; we can provision a dedicated connection pool slice to guarantee parallelism for the pilot.
- Pilot offer: guarantee 200 sustained concurrent short requests + 180 streaming sessions with a 1.5x burst allowance (up to 300 short-request concurrency and 270 streams for 3-minute bursts) for the first 30 days.
- Credits: we can include a one-time usage credit that offsets initial burst overage while we tune batching and KV caching for your workload.

Next steps
1) I attached a short matrix (redwood-connpool-options-20271201.pdf) that describes three capacity slices (baseline, pilot, dedicated) and the corresponding rate/connection thresholds. Please confirm which slice you'd like to start with.
2) Ben — could you draft the formal pilot terms and the credit amount we can offer?
3) Seth — can you share the fastledger-poc-reqs.xlsx (token estimates per call + typical token distribution) so we can finalize costs?

I’ll follow up with a proposed pilot start date after we get the file and Ben’s note.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]

From: Seth Li <seth.li@fastledger.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@fastledger.com
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 12:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: connection pooling thresholds, concurrency targets, and credits

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our engineering and procurement side:

Engineer's notes (from Ravi, copied here inline)
- 180 long-lived streams is accurate for active UI sessions during peak close. Those streams are small per-second token-wise but must stay very low-latency.
- Batch fanout: 600 parallel requests is the upper bound when we fan out to 20 partners concurrently. Typical fanout is 320–420 during mid-peak.
- We currently use HTTP/2 multiplexing on our connection pool; if Redwood supports session multiplexing we'd prefer to reuse fewer sockets.

Questions:
1) For the pilot burst allowance, is that enforced at the per-tenant routing layer (i.e., guaranteed) or best-effort with soft throttles?
2) If we exceed the burst cap during a real incident, what automatic fallbacks does Redwood provide (queued retry, 429s, model downgrade)?
3) Can you confirm whether streaming sessions count against the same concurrency bucket as short-lived generation requests?

Procurement note
- We need the pilot credit written into the SOW. Please propose a numeric credit amount so we can evaluate.

I'll upload the token distribution spreadsheet by EOD.

—Seth
Seth Li
Director, Infrastructure — FastLedger, Inc.
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Seth Li <seth.li@fastledger.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2027 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: connection pooling thresholds, concurrency targets, and credits

Hi Seth — Ben here (Infra/Product Partnerships). Short answers up front, then specifics.

Summary answers
- Burst allowance is a hard-configured routing policy for the pilot if you select the "pilot" capacity slice. That means we reserve extra headroom and will not throttle you to the baseline rate during the configured burst window.
- If you exceed the configured pilot burst, fallback behavior is: 1) short-lived requests beyond burst return 429; 2) streaming sessions beyond the guaranteed streams will be allowed to remain connected for a short drain period (30–90s) but new streams will be rejected with a 503; 3) automated model downgrade is available as an emergency policy but requires pre-approval in the SOW.
- Streaming sessions are counted against the streaming pool; short-lived generation requests are counted against the short-request pool. We maintain separate buckets but they share an overall tenant rate cap that can be expanded for Dedicated or pilot slices.

Technical details
- Connection pooling: we support HTTP/1.1 keep-alive and HTTP/2 multiplexing. For FastLedger’s HTTP/2 multiplexing, we recommend keeping per-socket concurrent streams <= 100 to avoid head-of-line contention across partner fanouts.
- Suggested config for pilot: set client-side socket_max_concurrent_streams to 96, keep-alive timeout 120s, and prefer reusing a small number of sockets (6–8) from each application instance. Redwood will bind those requests into the pilot short-request concurrency pool.
- Burst window policy: 3-minute sliding window with token bucket smoothing; pilot gives 1.5x burst on short-requests and 1.5x on streaming session creation for that window.

Credit proposal for SOW
- We can offer a $15k one-time credit to offset initial burst overage during the first 30 days of the pilot. If you prefer a usage-based trial instead, we can do $10k credit + 30 days of expanded telemetry and engineering support.

I'll draft the short SOW language and send a tracked version to procurement. Jordan — can you confirm FastLedger will accept separate streaming and short-request buckets in the first pass? Also looping Marissa to coordinate commercial terms.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Infra Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Attachment references: redwood-connpool-options-20271201.pdf (capacity matrix)
From: Seth Li <seth.li@fastledger.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: connection pooling thresholds, concurrency targets, and credits

Thanks Ben — that level of detail helps. FastLedger is comfortable starting with the pilot slice and the separate buckets as you described. A few quick confirmations before procurement signs: 

- Pilot start: prefer Dec 15 so we can finish an internal smoke test.
- Credit: we prefer the $15k one-time credit in the SOW. Procurement will expect a short clause that defines "burst window" and the exact enforcement behaviors (429 vs 503, drain period).
- Multiplexing guidance: we'll set socket_max_concurrent_streams to 96 per your recommendation and will reuse sockets on our side.

I'll upload the token spreadsheet (attached) and procurement will expect the tracked SOW by EOD Monday.

Next steps (action owners)
- Jordan: update HubSpot and send pilot start date proposal (Dec 15) and SOW draft link.
- Ben: send tracked SOW with the credit clause and burst enforcement language.
- Marissa: coordinate onboarding engineering contact and calendar for smoke test.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Seth
